children.translated_text: Having bowed his head to the god <s>Gaṇanātha Vināyaka</s>,

children.text: lokānāṃ ca vinodāya kariṣyāmi kathām imām ||
children.translated_text: I shall compose this story for the delight of people.
The lowly do not even begin, out of fear of obstacles;
middling people begin, but stop midway when obstacles arise.
But people of excellent qualities, even when struck by obstacles multiplied a thousandfold,
do not abandon what they have begun.

children.text: kecit prāñjalim icchanti kecid vakraṃ vaco budhāḥ
children.translated_text: Some wise people desire folded-hand reverence; some desire speech with a twist;

children.text: kecit kathāṃ rasasphītām ataḥ sarvaṃ vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: some desire a story swollen with rasa. Therefore all of this is being provided.

children.text: asti dakṣiṇāpathe janapade pratiṣṭhānaṃ nāma nagaram tatra vikramaseno nāma rājā ||
children.translated_text: In the southern country there is a city named <s>Pratiṣṭhāna</s>. There a king named <s>Vikramasena</s> lived.
What sort of king was he?
He shone like ten million suns and had a radiance equal to the light of lightning;
he sat on a splendid and charming throne, attended by his circle of ministers.
He was rich in beauty like <s>Kandarpa</s>, beloved of the people like <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: samudra iva maryādī samānaḥ sarvadā satām ||
children.translated_text: bounded in propriety like the ocean, and always impartial toward the good.
His splendor was like snow, jasmine, and the moon; he was spotless like the cool autumn moon;
he had the luster of a white lotus and the purity of clear crystal.
He was always intent on many kinds of gifts and devoted to many kinds of <s>dharma</s> (righteous conduct);
in anger he was like the fire of dissolution, with a brilliance like ten million flashes of lightning.
Endowed with abundant beauty and vigor, energetic and powerful,
rich in blazing rays of splendor, he became the delight of his lineage.

children.text: sādhūnāṃ pālanaṃ samyag duṣṭānāṃ nigrahas tathā
children.translated_text: Proper protection of the good, and likewise restraint of the wicked:

children.text: eṣa rājñāṃ paro dharmaḥ paratreha ca śarmaṇe ||
children.translated_text: this is the supreme <s>dharma</s> of kings, bringing happiness in the next world and in this one.

children.text: evaṃ guṇasamāviṣṭo rājā sarvāvasaram āsthāna upaviṣṭo'sti ||
children.translated_text: Endowed with such virtues, the king was seated in the assembly hall at the time open to all petitioners.

children.text: kasmiṃścid divase kuto 'pi sthānācchāntiśīlo nāma yogī digambaraḥ samāyātaḥ phalahastaḥ san sabhāṃ praviśya rājño haste phalaṃ dattavān ||
children.translated_text: One day, from some place or other, a naked yogin named <s>Śāntiśīla</s> arrived, carrying a fruit in his hand; entering the court, he gave the fruit into the king's hand.
The king gave him a seat and betel.

children.text: sa tu kṣaṇam āsane sthitvā tato nijamārge gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: But he sat on the seat for a moment and then went on his own way.

children.text: anayā rītyā rājño haste phalaṃ dattvā pratyahaṃ darśanaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: In this manner, giving a fruit into the king's hand, he came to see him every day.

children.text: ekasmin divase rājño hastāt patitaṃ phalaṃ markaṭena vidāritam tanmadhyād ratnam ekaṃ bhūmau nipatitam tasya kāntyā mahān uddyoto jātaḥ sarve'pi lokāḥ savismayāḥ saṃjātāḥ ||
children.translated_text: One day a fruit that had fallen from the king's hand was split open by a monkey. From inside it a single jewel fell to the ground, and from its brilliance a great radiance arose; all the people were filled with amazement.

children.text: tadā rājā sāścaryo babhūva rājñoktam bho digambara mahad ratnaṃ tvayā kena kāraṇenānītam ||
children.translated_text: Then the king became astonished and said, 'O naked ascetic, for what reason have you brought this great jewel?'

children.text: tadā digambareṇoktam mahārāja śrūyatām śāstre kathitam asti
children.translated_text: Then the naked ascetic said, 'Great king, listen. It is said in the śāstra:',

children.text: riktapāṇir na paśyeta rājānaṃ bhiṣajaṃ gurum
children.translated_text: 'One should not look upon a king, a physician, or a guru empty-handed,

children.text: daivajñaṃ putrakaṃ mitraṃ phalena phalam ādiśet ||
children.translated_text: nor an astrologer, a son, or a friend; with fruit one should indicate a result.'

children.text: mahārāja mayā anekānīdṛśāni ratnāni phalamadhyasthitāni dvādaśavarṣaparyantaṃ tava haste samarpitāni ||
children.translated_text: 'Great king, for twelve years I have presented into your hand many such jewels placed inside fruits.'

children.text: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rājñā bhāṇḍāgārika ākāritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Hearing that statement of his, the king summoned the treasurer.

children.text: rājñoktam bho bhāṇḍāgārika anena digambareṇa dattāni yāni phalāni tvayā bhāṇḍāgāre kṣiptāni tāni sarvāṇyānaya ||
children.translated_text: The king said, 'O treasurer, bring all those fruits given by this naked ascetic that you put in the treasury.'

children.text: rājño vacanaṃ śrutvā tenānītāni pratyekam utkṛṣya dṛṣṭāni sarvāṇy api ratnaiḥ pūrṇāni rājā ca hṛṣṭamanāḥ saṃjātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Hearing the king's command, he brought them. Each one was cut open and inspected, and all were full of jewels; the king became delighted in mind.

children.text: tato rājñā ratnasamūhaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhaṇitam bho digambara etāni sarvāṇi ratnāni bahumūlyāni kimartham ānītāni aham ekasyāpi ratnasya maulyaṃ dātum asamarthaḥ tvam ataḥ paraṃ kim abhilaṣasi tat kathaya ||
children.translated_text: Then, seeing the heap of jewels, the king said, 'O naked ascetic, all these jewels are very valuable. Why have they been brought? I am unable to pay the price of even one jewel. Tell me what you desire from now on.'
The yogin said:

children.text: api svalpataraṃ kāryaṃ yadi syāt pṛthivīpateḥ
children.translated_text: 'Even if a king's business should be very small,
it should not be spoken of in the midst of the assembly; <s>Bṛhaspati</s> has declared this.'
'A perfected mantra, a medicine, <s>dharma</s>, a household secret, sexual union,

children.text: kubhuktaṃ kuśrutaṃ marma matimān na prakāśayet ||
children.translated_text: bad eating, bad hearing, a vulnerable point: a wise man should not reveal these.'

children.text: ṣaṭkarṇo bhidyate mantraś caturkarṇaḥ sthiro bhavet
children.translated_text: 'A counsel heard by six ears is broken; one heard by four ears may remain firm;

children.text: dvikarṇasya tu mantrasya brahmāpyantaṃ na gacchati ||
children.translated_text: but of a counsel heard by two ears, even <s>Brahmā</s> does not reach the end.'

children.text: giripṛṣṭhaṃ samāruhya prāsāde vā raho gataḥ
children.translated_text: 'Having climbed a mountain slope, or having gone secretly into a palace,

children.text: araṇye nirjane sthāne tatra mantro vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: or in a lonely place in the forest, there counsel should be undertaken.'
'Lord, I shall inform you in private.'

children.text: rājñā nirjanaṃ kṛtam yoginoktam deva asyāṃ kṛṣṇacaturdaśyāṃ godānadītīre mahāśmaśāne mantrasādhanaṃ kariṣyāmi ||
children.translated_text: The king had the place emptied of people. The yogin said, 'Lord, on this dark fourteenth lunar day, on the bank of the <s>Godā</s> river, in the great cremation ground, I shall perform a mantra rite.'
'When it has been accomplished, the eight great siddhis will arise.'

children.text: aṇimā mahimā caiva laghimā garimā tathā
children.translated_text: 'Aṇimā, mahimā, laghimā, and garimā,

children.text: prāptiḥ prākāmyam īśitvaṃ vaśitvaṃ cāṣṭa siddhayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: prāpti, prākāmya, īśitva, and vaśitva: these are the eight siddhis.'
'A man who is endowed with courage becomes the assisting practitioner,
because a coward destroys even a perfected mantra.'

children.text: dhīras tu tvadṛte nānyaḥ puruṣaḥ pratibhāti me
children.translated_text: 'Apart from you, no other steadfast man appears to me;
therefore I wish to make you alone the assisting practitioner.'
'For that purpose, be my assisting practitioner.'

children.text: rātrau sakhaḍgena bhavatā ekākinā matsamīpam āgantavyam ||
children.translated_text: 'At night you must come near me alone, with your sword.'
The king agreed: 'I shall do so.'

children.text: tadanantaraṃ sarvopaskaradravyāṇi gṛhītvā digambaraś caturdaśyāṃ mahāśmaśāne gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: After that, taking all the necessary materials and substances, the naked ascetic went on the fourteenth lunar day to the great cremation ground.

children.text: rājāpi rajanyāṃ kṛṣṇavāsāṃsi gṛhītvā tatraiva samāyātaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The king too, at night, put on black garments and came to that very place.
When he saw the king, the ascetic's hair stood on end with joy.

children.text: yoginoktam bho rājan yojanārdhe mahāśmaśānam asti tatra śiṃśipāvṛkṣe mṛtakam avalambitam āste tatra gatvā tan mṛtakaṃ gṛhītvā śīghram āgaccha ||
children.translated_text: The yogin said: "O king, half a yojana away there is a great cremation ground. There, on a <s>śiṃśipā</s> tree, a corpse is hanging. Go there, take that corpse, and come back quickly."

children.text: yadi vadasi tarhi tanmṛtakaṃ punar vṛkṣe yāsyati ||
children.translated_text: "If you speak, then that corpse will go back to the tree again."

children.text: tad vacanam ākarṇya asamasāhasiko rājā śiṃśipāvṛkṣasyopari pracalitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having heard those words, the king, whose courage was unequaled, set out toward the <s>śiṃśipā</s> tree.
The king reached the cremation ground, fearless, amid dense smoke.
Furnished with every dreadful implement, the cremation ground shone upon the earth.
Its rampart was of white bones smeared with brains, and its reservoirs were blood.
It was like the playground of Death, crowded with skulls used as cups.
Darkened and stained by smoke, it thundered with the cries of demons.
It rose like a cloud of doom, flashed through by the flickering lightning of funeral-pyre fires.
With garlands of entrails dragged by vultures, it had the appearance of hanging festoons.
It was like Death himself, drunk at a festival and shaken by the dance of the Kṛttikās.
Winds arose there, rushing through the holes in old bone-tubes.
It seemed to resound with the anklets of bands of wandering yoginīs.
In the quarters echoed the terrible, swelling cries of jackals.
Like the destroyer making the syllable oṃ at the beginning of the dissolution of the three worlds,
it was adorned with fragments of severed heads and garlanded with heaps of skeletons.
Blackened by burning embers, it was like a second <s>Bhairava</s>.
It rang with cries raised like arrows in the ear and was filled with the slaughter of Duḥśāsana.
With terrifying men moving about, it was like a second <s>Bhārata</s>.

children.text: bahuchalaṃ dyūtam iva strīcittam iva dāruṇam
children.translated_text: It was very unstable like gambling, and cruel like the heart of a woman.
Like lack of discernment, it was a dwelling-place of many doubts and terrors.
Its inhabitants were harsh-voiced, and it was surrounded by dreadful Śūrpaṇakhās.
It resembled the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest, with <s>Mārīca</s> lurking fearfully within.
It was bewildering, shaking, with Dhūmrākṣa, Meghanāda, and Vibhīṣaṇa as terrors.
It seemed like the burning of <s>Laṅkā</s> itself, producing obstacles for the living <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
It was the abode of every sorrow and the assaulting ground of hosts of spirits.
It was tightly packed with many pits and continuously filled with masses of ghosts.
There, with mouths filled with flesh and minds delighted by liquor,
spirits, vetālas, and rākṣasas were seen in many forms.

children.text: tatra gatvā rājñā śiṃśipāvṛkṣam āruhya churikayā pāśaṃ chittvā mṛtakaṃ bhūtale pātitam ||
children.translated_text: Having gone there, the king climbed the <s>śiṃśipā</s> tree, cut the noose with his knife, and dropped the corpse to the ground.
What was the corpse like?
It was like a dark rain cloud, with hair standing upward, terrifying,
round-eyed, fleshless, and adorned with the marks of a ghost.

children.text: uttīrṇo yāvad rājā tāvanmṛtakaṃ tatraiva śākhāyām avalambitam ||
children.translated_text: As soon as the king had climbed down, the corpse was hanging again on that very branch.

children.text: punar api rājā vṛkṣam āruhya mṛtakaṃ skandhe dhṛtvā uttīrya mārge calitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Again the king climbed the tree, took the corpse on his shoulder, descended, and set out along the road.

children.text: mārge calite sati śavasaṃkramitena vetālena rājānaṃ pratyabhihitam bho rājan
children.translated_text: As he was walking on the road, the vetāla that had entered the corpse spoke to the king: "O king,
for the wise, time passes in the enjoyment of poetry and śāstra;

children.text: vyasanena tu mūrkhāṇāṃ nidrayā kalahena vā ||
children.translated_text: but for fools it passes in vice, sleep, or quarrel.

children.text: vinayena vinā kā śrīḥ kā niśā śaśinā vinā
children.translated_text: What is splendor without discipline? What is night without the moon?
And what sort of cleverness in speech is there if it is devoid of good poetry?

children.text: rājan śrūyatām tāvat kathām ekāṃ kathayāmi ||
children.translated_text: King, listen now; I shall tell one story."

children.text: ugraṃ bhayāvaharūpaṃ bhayaghnaṃ bhayasūdanaṃ mahābhīmaṃ mahānandaṃ namāmi gaṇanāyakam ||
children.translated_text: I bow to the lord of hosts, fierce, terrifying in form, remover of fear, destroyer of fear, greatly formidable, and greatly blissful.

children.text: punas tena rājñā śiṃśipāvṛkṣān mṛtakaṃ samānīya skandhe dhṛtvā yāvanmārge gacchati tāvat tena kathānakaṃ prārabdham ||
children.translated_text: Again, when that king had brought the corpse from the <s>śiṃśipā</s> tree, placed it on his shoulder, and was going along the road, the tale was begun by it.
The vetāla said: "King, listen; I shall tell a story.
There is a city named <s>Dharmapurī</s>.
There a king named <s>Dharmaśīla</s> lived.

children.text: tena caṇḍikāyatanaṃ kāritam agre caturaśraṃ kuṇḍaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: He had a shrine of <s>Caṇḍikā</s> made, and in front of it a square pit.

children.text: nityam eva devīṃ pūjayitvā bhojanaṃ karoti mantriṇoktam deva mama vacanaṃ śrūyatām
children.translated_text: Each day he worshipped the goddess and then took his meal. His minister said: 'Lord, hear my words.

children.text: aputrasya gṛhaṃ śūnyaṃ dik śūnyābāndhavasya ca
children.translated_text: The house of a man without a son is empty, and the quarter of one without kinsmen is empty.
The heart of a fool is empty, and poverty makes everything empty.'

children.text: evaṃ mantrivacanaṃ śrutvā rājñā devyāḥ stutir ārabdhā
children.translated_text: Having heard these words of the minister, the king began a hymn to the goddess:
'Homage to you, goddess, lady of the gods, worshipped by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Indra.
Born from the body of Śiva, gentle one, great Lakṣmī, homage to you.
Victory, goddess, greatly terrible one, fond of offerings of blood and flesh.
Form of Time, terrible as Time, dark night of Time, homage to you.
Mounted on a seat of great ghosts, fearsome even to Śiva,
wearing hide and severed heads, fierce one, four-faced one, homage, homage to you.

children.text: tālajaṅghe iti mahākāye stavena devī nirmāṃse samārādhitā māṃsabhakṣiṇi
children.translated_text: O long-legged, great-bodied one: by this hymn the fleshless, flesh-eating goddess was propitiated.
The goddess said:

children.text: ūrdhvakeśotkaṭe tuṣṭāhaṃ ūrdhvakeśotkaṭe tuṣṭāhaṃ ūrdhvakeśotkaṭe tava kṣāme rājendra tārakākṣi rājendra namo varaṃ brūhi 'stu yathepsitam
children.translated_text: 'With hair standing upward, I am pleased; with hair standing upward, I am pleased. With your fierce upward hair, O emaciated lord of kings, star-eyed lord of kings, homage; choose the boon you desire.'
to you.
What is desired.
